blocks.text: Ushering is effectively a paramilitary group within the church, responsible for security, orderliness, and protocol at every church event. Their responsibilities are extensive, and the group is led by a Head Usher.

items: Welcoming members, guests, and visitors, and politely directing them to their seats.
Preparing venues before events start - cleaning, arranging seats and furniture, and ensuring good aesthetics.
Assisting with sanitation and cleaning of the venue before, during, and after events.
Monitoring and maintaining orderliness of movement and conduct during events.
Collecting all offerings during events, and counting and recording them accurately.
Handing checked offerings over to designated officers for prompt banking.
Attending to the needs of the congregation during an ongoing event.
Taking attendance at events and services, and recording it as required.
Assisting with checking and evaluating church inventory.
Keeping careful custody of past and present records and statistics of church events.
Running errands for Pastors and Ministers to meet official needs during and after events.
Providing regular reports of the department's activities to the Pastorate.
Material contentment - since ushers handle offerings, anyone without a stable livelihood or unable to resist temptation should not volunteer for this role.
Humility and patience - ushers interact directly with people of every temperament and mood, and must receive all of them well.
A cheerful attitude - the usher is often the first person met at an event, and the person turned to for help, so a warm, sweet temperament matters regardless of personal circumstances.
A neat, attractive appearance - first impressions matter, and this affects the atmosphere of the whole event.
Sound ethics - usher conduct is guided by both stated and implied regulations.
Stamina and alertness - most ushering work involves standing or moving continuously while staying alert.
A prayerful spirit - ushers rarely close their eyes even during prayer, but should remain prayerful so the Holy Spirit can move freely.
Being smart and personable - people respond well to being understood and treated with honour.
Endurance - ushers are typically the first to arrive and the last to leave.
Security consciousness - not everyone who attends a church event comes with good motives, and an usher should be alert to this.
